content:
The first few minutes of first lady Melania Trump’s new docuseries offers a glimpse into her dynamic with President Donald Trump — and woof.

The tension between the first couple is palpable just in the opening credits of “Melania: The Series,” the first lady’s follow-up to her widely panned eponymous film that premiered on streaming Friday. In the intro, audio of Melania Trump can be heard saying, “I don’t agree with everything my husband does” as footage of the president doing his signature “YMCA” dance plays on the screen.

Things get even spicier in the opening scene of the episode, titled “Family & Trust,” in which the couple sits down for a joint interview with an unseen person associated with the Amazon MGM show.

The couple is asked by the interviewer, “Who is more difficult, you or her?”

Donald Trump declares that he’s “much easier” to get along with than the public thinks. Then adds, “She could very well be more difficult.”

During this exchange, Melania Trump plays nice by laughing at her husband’s slight. But the next scene features a follow-up interview with the first lady aboard a private jet, in which she’s fuming as she reflects on Trump’s dig.

“He said, like, ‘Oh, she’s so difficult,’” Melania Trump retorts. “But I tell him the truth. I feel that sometimes there are too many people around him, that they are ‘yes people,’ and that’s not healthy.”

The show then cuts back to the couple’s joint interview, in which the president says:

“She feels very strongly that everything should be very presidential. And when we were doing rallies, if, on occasion, I’d break into a dance, I’m not sure she loved it so much.”

This seems like a sore subject for the couple, considering that Donald Trump has openly admitted in the past that the first lady is not a fan of his weird little hand-jerk dance.

Again, sitting next to her husband, Melania Trump makes an effort to be more diplomatic during the joint interview.

“Well, sometimes, ya know, the situations were like, uh, I don’t think it’s a good day to dance. So,” she says.

The episode then moves on to Melania Trump explaining that one of her biggest responsibilities as first lady is handling “so many schedules.”

“I feel like I know what my husband is doing, and what my son [Baron Trump] is doing, but I don’t think they know what I’m doing,” Melania Trump says with a laugh.

Here’s hoping that some producer on “Melania: The Series” decides to give her a copy of “The Feminine Mystique” and makes this show even more uncomfortable to watch.

“Melania: The Series” is now streaming on Amazon Prime Video, if this article somehow made you interested in watching it.
